case.question: Bank of Mexico decreases interest rates by 25 bps after November 2026 meeting?

minutes.vote: All five named members voted unanimously to maintain the overnight interbank target at 6.50%: Victoria Rodríguez Ceja, Galia Borja Gómez, José Gabriel Cuadra García, Jonathan Ernest Heath Constable, Omar Mejía Castelazo.
minutes.common_guidance: Future decisions depend on continued disinflation and its determinants, including FX pass-through, slack and inflation expectations; Banxico need not follow anticipated Fed moves mechanically.
member_forward_guidance_differences: One member said upcoming decisions could consider a one-off rate decrease if inflation and its determinants continued supporting disinflation.
One supported case-by-case decisions without a predetermined path; a cut could be considered if inflation evolves favorably and financial markets remain orderly.
One urged keeping rates at current levels for a prolonged period and warned a Fed-cycle decoupling would depend on Mexico consolidating convergence to 3%.
One said a downward fine-tuning discussion could remain open, not anticipated, conditional on falling inflation and orderly financial conditions.
Another emphasized caution, upside risks and monitoring firmly anchored expectations while holding unchanged.

banxico_expectations_survey.classification: private-sector forecast survey, not realized inflation; response window crosses the Sep 23 Board session and announcement date.

timing_limit: The Sep CPI release and Sep expectations survey were published after the Sep 23/24 meeting. Survey responses extend through Sep 28; do not treat these as all information available to that Board session.
scope: Factual supplement only; no probability or market-price inspection.
